llm_findings: Single causal change: only --clip-after-reduce is added. Authoritative train.py lines 6352–6367 describe precisely the local-clip-before-AVG versus averaged-gradient clipping change; existing separate n-gram clipping is preserved.

The static default concern is resolved by the supplied evidence: train.py sets CLIP_AFTER_REDUCE=False, and argparse uses that default unless NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_CLIP_AFTER_REDUCE overrides it. Neither pinned control environment contains that override.

Repository evidence supports an experiment, not an established win: fs-w16 reports 0.981174 BPB/3005 steps versus fs-w12 at 0.981710/2977. Their commits differ, fs-w16's box is unspecified, and fs-w16 additionally spells out --pack-factor 4, so the claim of identical literal flag sets minus clipping is inaccurate.

No supplied decision-log entry closes this clip-order test on the 592.9M default configuration. Prior dense-model clip-order work is acknowledged and is materially distinct from testing transfer to the n-gram-enabled defaults.
Competition-legal scope: this changes training-loop optimizer behavior only, with no pretrained weights, external data, tokenizer changes, or evaluator changes.

The seed-42 matched full-chip experiment is falsifiable through the predeclared public-BPB improvement threshold and step-count outcome classes. Throughput neutrality remains a prediction, not a construction guarantee; the 0.0003 inert band is a chosen tolerance, not an established statistical noise floor from two cross-box controls. The proposal appropriately separates fixed-budget improvement from proof of the variance mechanism.
